headline: Directs the Treasury to mint a commemorative $1 silver coin marking the WWI centennial, sold only in 2018, with a design contest and a $10 surcharge per coin.
what_it_does: The law tells the Treasury Secretary to make and sell $1 silver coins honoring the 100th anniversary of America's entry into World War I. It also requires a juried design contest for the coin's front and back, with a paid prize for the winner. The coins may only be issued during calendar year 2018, and each coin sold carries a $10 surcharge that goes to the United States Foundation for the Commemoration of the World Wars to support the World War I Centennial Commission. The Treasury must make sure the program costs the government nothing, and surcharge money is not paid out until the coin's design and issuing costs are recovered.

who_it_affects.how: They can purchase the special silver coin during 2018, but each one carries a $10 surcharge on top of its face value.

who_it_affects.group: World War I veterans and their families
who_it_affects.how: The coin and its surcharge funds are meant to help commemorate the war's centennial.

who_it_affects.group: The World War I Centennial Commission and the United States Foundation for the Commemoration of the World Wars
who_it_affects.how: They receive surcharge money from coin sales to help fund centennial commemoration activities, after program costs are covered.

who_it_affects.group: Artists who enter the design competition
who_it_affects.how: They may submit designs in a juried contest, and the winner receives compensation.

when_it_takes_effect: Coins may be issued only during calendar year 2018, after the law was enacted on December 16, 2014.
